def _engine_to_json(state: _SymbolState) -> dict[str, object]:
    raw = state.engine.dump_state()
    return {
        "last_sequence": state.last_sequence,
        "event_log": [
            {"event_id": event_id, "content": content}
            for event_id, content in state.seen.items()
        ],
        "plans": [state.plans[plan_id].to_json() for plan_id in sorted(state.plans)],
        "engine": {
            "event_ids": sorted(raw["event_ids"]),
            "order_ids": sorted(raw["order_ids"]),
            "reserved_order_ids": sorted(raw["reserved_order_ids"]),
            "orders": {
                order_id: raw["orders"][order_id]
                for order_id in sorted(raw["orders"])
            },
            "bids": [
                {"price": price, "order_ids": list(queue)}
                for price, queue in sorted(raw["bids"].items())
            ],
            "asks": [
                {"price": price, "order_ids": list(queue)}
                for price, queue in sorted(raw["asks"].items())
            ],
            "bid_totals": {str(price): qty for price, qty in sorted(raw["bid_totals"].items())},
            "ask_totals": {str(price): qty for price, qty in sorted(raw["ask_totals"].items())},
            "next_trade_id": raw["next_trade_id"],
            "accounts": sorted(raw["accounts"]),
            "trade_log": raw["trade_log"],
        },
    }


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, message)


def _is_str_set_list(value: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)


def _non_negative_int(value: object) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0


def _parse_plan_entry(entry: dict[str, object]) -> "ExecutionPlan":
    """Validate one serialized plan record and rebuild the :class:`ExecutionPlan`."""

    def pos_int(name: str) -> int:
        value = entry.get(name)
        _require(
            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
            f"plan {entry.get('plan_id')!r} {name} must be a positive integer",
        )
        return value

    plan_id = entry.get("plan_id")
    _require(_is_non_empty_str(plan_id), "plan plan_id must be a non-empty string")
    side = entry.get("side")
    _require(side in (BUY, SELL), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad side")
    order_type = entry.get("order_type")
    _require(order_type in (LIMIT, MARKET), f"plan {plan_id} has a bad order type")
    benchmark_price = pos_int("benchmark_price")
    price = entry.get("price")
    if order_type == LIMIT:
        _require(
            isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
            f"plan {plan_id} LIMIT price must be a positive integer",
        )
    else:
        _require(price is None, f"plan {plan_id} MARKET must not carry a price")
    account_id = entry.get("account_id")
    _require(
        account_id is None or _is_non_empty_str(account_id),
        f"plan {plan_id} account_id is malformed",
    )
    raw_slices = entry.get("slice_quantities")
    _require(
        isinstance(raw_slices, list) and len(raw_slices) > 0,
        f"plan {plan_id} slice_quantities must be a non-empty list",
    )
    slice_quantities: list[int] = []
    for value in raw_slices:
        _require(
            isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
            f"plan {plan_id} slice quantities must be positive integers",
        )
        slice_quantities.append(value)
    released = entry.get("released")
    released_quantity = entry.get("released_quantity")
    filled_quantity = entry.get("filled_quantity")
    cancelled_quantity = entry.get("cancelled_quantity")
    notional = entry.get("notional")
    for name, value in (
        ("released", released),
        ("released_quantity", released_quantity),
        ("filled_quantity", filled_quantity),
        ("cancelled_quantity", cancelled_quantity),
        ("notional", notional),
    ):
        _require(_non_negative_int(value), f"plan {plan_id} {name} must be a non-negative integer")
    status = entry.get("status")
    _require(
        status in (PLAN_ACTIVE, PLAN_COMPLETED, PLAN_CANCELLED),
        f"plan {plan_id} has a bad status",
    )
    slice_count = len(slice_quantities)
    _require(0 <= released <= slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} released slice index out of range")
    total_quantity = sum(slice_quantities)
    _require(
        released_quantity == sum(slice_quantities[:released]),
        f"plan {plan_id} released_quantity does not match its slices",
    )
    _require(
        filled_quantity <= released_quantity,
        f"plan {plan_id} filled quantity exceeds released quantity",
    )
    if status == PLAN_ACTIVE:
        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE with no slices left")
        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is ACTIVE but carries cancellations")
    elif status == PLAN_COMPLETED:
        _require(released == slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED before all slices")
        _require(cancelled_quantity == 0, f"plan {plan_id} is COMPLETED but carries cancellations")
    else:
        _require(released < slice_count, f"plan {plan_id} is CANCELLED after all slices")
        _require(
            cancelled_quantity == total_quantity - released_quantity,
            f"plan {plan_id} cancelled quantity does not cover the unreleased remainder",
        )

    plan = ExecutionPlan.__new__(ExecutionPlan)
    plan.plan_id = plan_id
    plan.side = side
    plan.order_type = order_type
    plan.benchmark_price = benchmark_price
    plan.price = price
    plan.account_id = account_id
    plan.slice_quantities = slice_quantities
    plan.released = released
    plan.released_quantity = released_quantity
    plan.filled_quantity = filled_quantity
    plan.cancelled_quantity = cancelled_quantity
    plan.notional = notional
    plan.status = status
    return plan


_ORDER_RECORD_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"side", "price", "remaining", "status", "account_id",
     "display_quantity", "visible"}
)
_TRADE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"trade_id", "maker_order_id", "taker_order_id", "price", "quantity", "event_id"}
)
_SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS = frozenset({"last_sequence", "event_log", "plans", "engine"})
_ENGINE_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"event_ids", "order_ids", "reserved_order_ids", "orders", "bids", "asks",
     "bid_totals", "ask_totals", "next_trade_id", "accounts", "trade_log"}
)
_PLAN_KEYS = frozenset(
    {"plan_id", "side", "order_type", "benchmark_price", "price", "account_id",
     "slice_quantities", "released", "released_quantity", "filled_quantity",
     "cancelled_quantity", "notional", "status"}
)
_ENVELOPE_KEYS_SNAPSHOT = frozenset(
    {"format_version", "engine_version", "config", "config_digest",
     "content", "content_digest"}
)
_CONTENT_KEYS = frozenset({"symbols", "events"})


def _engine_from_json(data: dict[str, object]) -> _SymbolState:
    _require(isinstance(data, dict), "symbol state must be an object")
    _require(set(data) == _SYMBOL_STATE_KEYS, "symbol state has unknown fields")
    last_sequence = data.get("last_sequence")
    _require(
        isinstance(last_sequence, int) and not isinstance(last_sequence, bool) and last_sequence >= 0,
        "last_sequence must be a non-negative integer",
    )
    event_log = data.get("event_log")
    _require(isinstance(event_log, list), "event_log must be a list")
    seen: dict[str, str] = {}
    for entry in event_log:
        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "event_log entry must be an object")
        _require(set(entry) == {"event_id", "content"},
                 "event_log entry has unknown fields")
        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
        content = entry.get("content")
        _require(isinstance(event_id, str) and isinstance(content, str),
                 "event_log entry fields have wrong types")
        _require(event_id not in seen, "duplicate event id in symbol event log")
        seen[event_id] = content

    # Partition the accepted events into baseline engine events and TWAP
    # command events: the engine journal only knows the former plus the child
    # orders synthesized for released slices, while every TWAP command id lives
    # solely in the replay log.
    baseline_event_ids: set[str] = set()
    twap_event_ids: set[str] = set()
    for event_id, content in seen.items():
        try:
            stored_type = json.loads(content).get("type")
        except (ValueError, AttributeError):
            _require(False, f"event log content for {event_id} is not a JSON object")
            stored_type = None
        if stored_type in _TWAP_TYPES:
            twap_event_ids.add(event_id)
        else:
            baseline_event_ids.add(event_id)

    plans_raw = data.get("plans")
    _require(isinstance(plans_raw, list), "plans must be a list")
    plans: dict[str, ExecutionPlan] = {}
    plan_index: dict[str, str] = {}
    released_child_ids: set[str] = set()
    reserved_child_ids: set[str] = set()
    for entry in plans_raw:
        _require(isinstance(entry, dict), "plan entry must be an object")
        _require(set(entry) == _PLAN_KEYS, "plan entry has unknown fields")
        plan = _parse_plan_entry(entry)
        plan_id = plan.plan_id
        _require(plan_id not in plans, f"duplicate execution plan id {plan_id}")
        for index in range(plan.slice_count):
            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
            _require(
                child_id not in plan_index,
                f"derived order id {child_id} is claimed by two plans",
            )
            plan_index[child_id] = plan_id
            if index < plan.released:
                released_child_ids.add(child_id)
            else:
                reserved_child_ids.add(child_id)
        plans[plan_id] = plan

    engine_data = data.get("engine")
    _require(isinstance(engine_data, dict), "engine state must be an object")
    _require(set(engine_data) == _ENGINE_KEYS, "engine state has unknown fields")

    event_ids = engine_data.get("event_ids")
    order_ids = engine_data.get("order_ids")
    reserved_raw = engine_data.get("reserved_order_ids")
    accounts = engine_data.get("accounts")
    _require(_is_str_set_list(event_ids), "engine.event_ids must be a list of strings")
    _require(_is_str_set_list(order_ids), "engine.order_ids must be a list of strings")
    _require(
        _is_str_set_list(reserved_raw),
        "engine.reserved_order_ids must be a list of strings",
    )
    _require(_is_str_set_list(accounts), "engine.accounts must be a list of strings")
    _require(
        set(reserved_raw) == reserved_child_ids,
        "reserved order ids do not match the plans' unreleased slices",
    )
    _require(
        set(reserved_raw).isdisjoint(order_ids),
        "an order id is both reserved and spent",
    )

    orders = engine_data.get("orders")
    _require(isinstance(orders, dict), "engine.orders must be an object")
    for order_id, record in orders.items():
        _require(isinstance(order_id, str) and isinstance(record, dict),
                 "engine.orders entries are malformed")
        _require(set(record) <= _ORDER_RECORD_KEYS,
                 f"order {order_id} has unknown fields")

    def parse_levels(raw_levels: object, raw_totals: object, side_name: str):
        _require(isinstance(raw_levels, list), f"{side_name} levels must be a list")
        levels: list[tuple[int, list[str]]] = []
        seen_prices: set[int] = set()
        for level in raw_levels:
            _require(isinstance(level, dict), f"{side_name} level must be an object")
            _require(set(level) == {"price", "order_ids"},
                     f"{side_name} level has unknown fields")
            price = level.get("price")
            ids = level.get("order_ids")
            _require(
                isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0,
                f"{side_name} level price must be a positive integer",
            )
            _require(_is_str_set_list(ids), f"{side_name} level order_ids must be strings")
            _require(price not in seen_prices, f"duplicate {side_name} price level")
            seen_prices.add(price)
            levels.append((price, ids))
        _require(isinstance(raw_totals, dict), f"{side_name} totals must be an object")
        totals: dict[int, int] = {}
        for price_text, qty in raw_totals.items():
            _require(isinstance(price_text, str), f"{side_name} total price key must be a string")
            try:
                price = int(price_text)
            except ValueError:
                _require(False, f"{side_name} total price key is not numeric")
            _require(str(price) == price_text and price > 0,
                     f"{side_name} total price key is not normalized")
            _require(isinstance(qty, int) and not isinstance(qty, bool) and qty > 0,
                     f"{side_name} total quantity must be a positive integer")
            totals[price] = qty
        _require(set(totals) == seen_prices,
                 f"{side_name} levels and aggregates disagree")
        return levels, totals

    bid_levels, bid_totals = parse_levels(
        engine_data.get("bids"), engine_data.get("bid_totals"), "bid"
    )
    ask_levels, ask_totals = parse_levels(
        engine_data.get("asks"), engine_data.get("ask_totals"), "ask"
    )

    bids = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in bid_levels}
    asks = {price: deque(ids) for price, ids in ask_levels}

    valid_status = {"FILLED", "RESTING", "CANCELLED"}
    for order_id, record in orders.items():
        side = record.get("side")
        status = record.get("status")
        remaining = record.get("remaining")
        price = record.get("price")
        _require(side in ("BUY", "SELL"), f"order {order_id} has a bad side")
        _require(status in valid_status, f"order {order_id} has a bad status")
        _require(
            isinstance(remaining, int) and not isinstance(remaining, bool) and remaining >= 0,
            f"order {order_id} remaining must be a non-negative integer",
        )
        _require(
            price is None or (isinstance(price, int) and not isinstance(price, bool) and price > 0),
            f"order {order_id} price is malformed",
        )
        if "account_id" in record:
            _require(isinstance(record["account_id"], str) and record["account_id"] != "",
                     f"order {order_id} account_id is malformed")
        if "display_quantity" in record or "visible" in record:
            # Iceberg records keep their peak size after they finish; a fully
            # filled record additionally carries a zero current slice, while a
            # cancelled one keeps the slice it had when removed.
            display_quantity = record.get("display_quantity")
            visible = record.get("visible")
            _require(
                isinstance(display_quantity, int) and not isinstance(display_quantity, bool)
                and display_quantity > 0,
                f"iceberg order {order_id} display_quantity is malformed",
            )
            _require(
                isinstance(visible, int) and not isinstance(visible, bool) and visible >= 0,
                f"iceberg order {order_id} visible slice is malformed",
            )
            if status == "RESTING":
                _require(visible > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no visible slice")
                _require(remaining > 0, f"resting iceberg {order_id} has no remainder")
                # The current slice may itself be partially consumed; it is only
                # reset to min(peak, remaining) once fully exhausted.
                _require(
                    visible <= min(display_quantity, remaining),
                    f"resting iceberg {order_id} slice exceeds peak or remainder",
                )
        else:
            _require(
                status != "RESTING" or remaining > 0,
                f"resting order {order_id} must have a positive remainder",
            )

    def check_level_aggregates(levels, totals, side_name):
        queued: set[str] = set()
        for price, ids in levels:
            level_visible = 0
            for order_id in ids:
                _require(order_id not in queued, f"order {order_id} queued twice")
                queued.add(order_id)
                record = orders.get(order_id)
                _require(record is not None, f"{side_name} queue references unknown order")
                level_visible += record.get("visible", record["remaining"])
            _require(level_visible == totals[price],
                     f"{side_name} aggregate at {price} does not match the queue")
        return queued

    bid_queued = check_level_aggregates(bid_levels, bid_totals, "bid")
    ask_queued = check_level_aggregates(ask_levels, ask_totals, "ask")
    _require(bid_queued.isdisjoint(ask_queued), "an order rests on both sides")

    # Every resting order is queued, and every finished order is not.
    resting = {oid for oid, rec in orders.items() if rec["status"] == "RESTING"}
    _require(resting == bid_queued | ask_queued,
             "resting orders and queued orders disagree")
    for order_id in bid_queued:
        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "BUY", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")
    for order_id in ask_queued:
        _require(orders[order_id]["side"] == "SELL", f"{order_id} rests on the wrong side")

    # The id sets mirror exactly what the baseline engine would hold. The
    # engine only knows baseline events and synthesized child orders; TWAP
    # command ids live solely in the replay layer's event log.
    _require(set(order_ids) == set(orders), "order_ids and order records disagree")
    _require(
        set(event_ids) == (baseline_event_ids - set(plan_index)) | released_child_ids,
        "engine event ids do not match the baseline events and released slices",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids <= set(order_ids),
        "a released plan slice is missing an engine order record",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
    )
    _require(last_sequence == len(seen),
             "last_sequence does not match the contiguous accepted event count")

    for record in orders.values():
        account_id = record.get("account_id")
        if account_id is not None:
            _require(account_id in accounts, f"account {account_id} missing from accounts")

    next_trade_id = engine_data.get("next_trade_id")
    _require(
        isinstance(next_trade_id, int) and not isinstance(next_trade_id, bool) and next_trade_id >= 1,
        "next_trade_id must be a positive integer",
    )

    trade_log = engine_data.get("trade_log")
    _require(isinstance(trade_log, list), "trade_log must be a list")
    expected_trade_id = 1
    for trade in trade_log:
        _require(isinstance(trade, dict), "trade log entry must be an object")
        _require(set(trade) == _TRADE_KEYS, "trade log entry has unknown fields")
        trade_id = trade.get("trade_id")
        _require(
            isinstance(trade_id, int) and not isinstance(trade_id, bool) and trade_id == expected_trade_id,
            "trade log ids must be consecutive from 1",
        )
        expected_trade_id += 1
        for key in ("maker_order_id", "taker_order_id", "event_id"):
            _require(isinstance(trade.get(key), str), f"trade log {key} must be a string")
        for key in ("price", "quantity"):
            value = trade.get(key)
            _require(
                isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0,
                f"trade log {key} must be a positive integer",
            )
    _require(next_trade_id == expected_trade_id,
             "next_trade_id does not match the cumulative trade log")

    # Historical trades may only reference orders and events that the engine
    # still considers accepted.
    for trade in trade_log:
        maker_id = trade["maker_order_id"]
        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
        trade_event_id = trade["event_id"]
        _require(maker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown maker {maker_id}")
        _require(taker_id in orders, f"trade references unknown taker {taker_id}")
        _require(trade_event_id in event_ids,
                 f"trade references unknown event {trade_event_id}")
        maker = orders[maker_id]
        taker = orders[taker_id]
        _require(maker["side"] != taker["side"], "a trade cannot join two same-side orders")

    # Cross-validate every plan against the engine journal and order records:
    # released child ids must denote IOC child orders with the plan's side and
    # account, the child's original quantity must equal its slice quantity, and
    # the cumulative filled quantity / notional must match the trades exactly.
    child_fill_qty: dict[str, int] = {}
    child_notional: dict[str, int] = {}
    for trade in trade_log:
        taker_id = trade["taker_order_id"]
        if taker_id in plan_index:
            child_fill_qty[taker_id] = child_fill_qty.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["quantity"]
            child_notional[taker_id] = (
                child_notional.get(taker_id, 0) + trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
            )
    for plan in plans.values():
        plan_filled = 0
        plan_notional = 0
        for index in range(plan.slice_count):
            child_id = plan.child_order_id(index + 1)
            if index >= plan.released:
                _require(
                    child_id not in orders,
                    f"plan {plan.plan_id} unreleased slice already has an order record",
                )
                continue
            record = orders[child_id]
            _require(record["side"] == plan.side,
                     f"child {child_id} trades on the wrong side")
            _require(record["status"] != "RESTING",
                     f"IOC child {child_id} must not rest in the book")
            _require(
                record["price"] == plan.price,
                f"child {child_id} price disagrees with its plan",
            )
            _require(
                record.get("account_id") == plan.account_id,
                f"child {child_id} account disagrees with its plan",
            )
            filled = child_fill_qty.get(child_id, 0)
            slice_quantity = plan.slice_quantities[index]
            _require(
                filled + record["remaining"] == slice_quantity,
                f"child {child_id} quantity does not match its plan slice",
            )
            plan_filled += filled
            plan_notional += child_notional.get(child_id, 0)
        _require(plan_filled == plan.filled_quantity,
                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} filled quantity disagrees with the trade log")
        _require(plan_notional == plan.notional,
                 f"plan {plan.plan_id} notional disagrees with the trade log")

    # Every derived id is either a released child order or an engine
    # reservation; no plan id may be missing on either side, and external
    # orders may never squat on a derived id.
    _require(
        set(plan_index) == released_child_ids | reserved_child_ids,
        "plan derived ids disagree with engine order state",
    )
    _require(
        released_child_ids.isdisjoint(reserved_child_ids),
        "a plan slice is both released and reserved",
    )

    # Deep copy so later caller mutation of the snapshot document can never
    # reach the live engine.
    engine = Engine(
        _state={
            "event_ids": set(event_ids),
            "order_ids": set(order_ids),
            "reserved_order_ids": set(reserved_raw),
            "orders": copy.deepcopy(orders),
            "bids": bids,
            "asks": asks,
            "bid_totals": bid_totals,
            "ask_totals": ask_totals,
            "next_trade_id": next_trade_id,
            "accounts": set(accounts),
            "trade_log": copy.deepcopy(trade_log),
        }
    )
    state = _SymbolState(engine)
    state.last_sequence = last_sequence
    state.seen = seen
    state.plans = plans
    state.plan_index = plan_index
    return state


def export_snapshot(replayer: EventReplayer) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Export a resumable, JSON-compatible snapshot of a replay session.

    The snapshot fully preserves (per security): price-time queue priority,
    order remainders, the iceberg current slice and replenishment state, the
    last sequence, cumulative trades and the next trade id counter. It also
    carries the format version, the matching configuration (plus its digest)
    and a SHA-256 digest over the normalized whole document.
    """
    symbols = [
        {"symbol": symbol, "state": _engine_to_json(replayer._symbols[symbol])}
        for symbol in sorted(replayer._symbols)
    ]
    content = {
        "symbols": symbols,
        "events": [
            {"event_id": event_id, "symbol": symbol, "content": content_str}
            for event_id, (symbol, content_str) in sorted(replayer._events.items())
        ],
    }
    envelope: dict[str, object] = {
        "format_version": FORMAT_VERSION,
        "engine_version": __version__,
        "config": replayer.config,
        "config_digest": replayer.config_digest,
        "content": content,
    }
    envelope["content_digest"] = _digest(
        {key: value for key, value in envelope.items() if key != "content_digest"}
    )
    return envelope


def restore_replayer(
    snapshot: dict[str, object],
    config: dict[str, object] | None = None,
) -> EventReplayer:
    """Rebuild an :class:`EventReplayer` from :func:`export_snapshot` output.

    Version, configuration digest and content SHA-256 are verified before any
    state is adopted. Any failure raises :class:`SnapshotError` and leaves no
    partially recovered session behind.
    """
    if not isinstance(snapshot, dict):
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot must be a JSON object")
    if not set(snapshot) <= _ENVELOPE_KEYS_SNAPSHOT:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot document has unknown fields")

    version = snapshot.get("format_version")
    if version != FORMAT_VERSION:
        raise SnapshotError(
            SNAPSHOT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED,
            f"unsupported snapshot format version: {version!r}",
        )
    engine_version = snapshot.get("engine_version")
    if not isinstance(engine_version, str) or engine_version == "":
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot engine_version is malformed")

    expected_config = DEFAULT_CONFIG if config is None else config
    snapshot_config = snapshot.get("config")
    if snapshot_config != expected_config:
        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration does not match")
    if snapshot.get("config_digest") != _digest(expected_config):
        raise SnapshotError(CONFIG_MISMATCH, "snapshot configuration digest does not match")

    stored_digest = snapshot.get("content_digest")
    actual_digest = _digest(
        {key: value for key, value in snapshot.items() if key != "content_digest"}
    )
    if not isinstance(stored_digest, str) or stored_digest != actual_digest:
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content digest mismatch")

    content = snapshot.get("content")
    if (
        not isinstance(content, dict)
        or set(content) != _CONTENT_KEYS
        or not isinstance(content.get("symbols"), list)
        or not isinstance(content.get("events"), list)
    ):
        raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot content is malformed")

    # Build the whole session in locals first; only commit it to the returned
    # object after every component parsed successfully.
    replayer = EventReplayer(expected_config)
    symbols: dict[str, _SymbolState] = {}
    events: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for entry in content["symbols"]:
        if not (
            isinstance(entry, dict)
            and set(entry) == {"symbol", "state"}
            and isinstance(entry.get("symbol"), str)
            and isinstance(entry.get("state"), dict)
        ):
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot symbol entry is malformed")
        symbol = entry["symbol"]
        if symbol in symbols:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate symbol in snapshot: {symbol}")
        try:
            symbols[symbol] = _engine_from_json(entry["state"])
        except (KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"snapshot state for {symbol} is malformed") from exc
    for entry in content.get("events", []):
        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != {"event_id", "symbol", "content"}:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log is malformed")
        event_id = entry.get("event_id")
        symbol = entry.get("symbol")
        text = entry.get("content")
        if not isinstance(event_id, str) or not isinstance(symbol, str) or not isinstance(text, str):
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, "snapshot event log entry is malformed")
        if symbol not in symbols:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"event {event_id} references unknown symbol")
        if event_id in events:
            raise SnapshotError(SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT, f"duplicate event id in snapshot: {event_id}")
        events[event_id] = (symbol, text)

    # The global event log and the per-symbol event logs must describe exactly
    # the same accepted events, with identical normalized content.
    logged_per_symbol: dict[str, int] = {}
    for symbol, text in events.values():
        logged_per_symbol[symbol] = logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) + 1
    for symbol, symbol_state in symbols.items():
        for event_id, text in symbol_state.seen.items():
            if events.get(event_id) != (symbol, text):
                raise SnapshotError(
                    SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
                    f"event {event_id} disagrees between global and symbol log",
                )
        if logged_per_symbol.get(symbol, 0) != len(symbol_state.seen):
            raise SnapshotError(
                SNAPSHOT_CORRUPT,
                f"event log counts disagree for symbol {symbol}",
            )

    replayer._symbols = symbols
    replayer._events = events
    return replayer


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public one-call entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def replay_events(
    events: list[dict[str, object]],
    config: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    snapshot: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    snapshot_after: object = "last",
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Replay one ordered multi-security event stream in a single public call.

    Parameters
    ----------
    events:
        Event objects in strict submission order. Each event carries
        ``event_id`` (non-empty string, unique across the whole stream),
        ``symbol`` (non-empty string), ``sequence`` (positive integer,
        strictly increasing per symbol) and a payload — either inline
        (``"type"`` plus the fields of that event kind) or nested under an
        ``"event"`` object that repeats ``event_id`` and ``type``. Supported
        kinds are the baseline ADD/CANCEL/REPLACE events and the TWAP
        TWAP_START/TWAP_SLICE/TWAP_CANCEL/TWAP_REPORT commands.
    config:
        Matching configuration summary. Defaults to :data:`DEFAULT_CONFIG`;
        a resumed run must pass the same configuration the snapshot carries.
    snapshot:
        Optional snapshot returned by an earlier :func:`export_snapshot` /
        :func:`replay_events` call. Restoration is fully verified before any
        event is processed.
    snapshot_after:
        ``"last"`` (default) attaches the snapshot after the final event;
        ``None`` omits it; ``{"symbol": ..., "sequence": ...}`` attaches the
        snapshot right after that identified successful event.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``{"results": [...], "snapshot": {...} | None}``. Each result is
        associated with ``event_id``/``symbol``/``sequence``, carries a
        ``status`` of ``ACCEPTED``, ``REJECTED`` or ``DUPLICATE`` (with
        ``rejection_code`` for rejections), and lists the event's trades,
        book changes and the post-event ``bids``/``asks``.
    """
    if not isinstance(events, list):
        raise TypeError("events must be a list of event objects")

    if snapshot is not None:
        replayer = restore_replayer(snapshot, config)
    else:
        replayer = EventReplayer(config)

    if snapshot_after is not None and snapshot_after != "last":
        if not (
            isinstance(snapshot_after, dict)
            and isinstance(snapshot_after.get("symbol"), str)
            and isinstance(snapshot_after.get("sequence"), int)
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "snapshot_after must be 'last', None or "
                "{'symbol': str, 'sequence': int}"
            )

    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
    exported: dict[str, object] | None = None
    marker_matched = snapshot_after is None or snapshot_after == "last"
    for position, event in enumerate(events):
        result = replayer._submit_one(event)
        results.append(result)
        if (
            snapshot_after is not None
            and snapshot_after != "last"
            and result.get("symbol") == snapshot_after["symbol"]
            and result.get("sequence") == snapshot_after["sequence"]
        ):
            marker_matched = True
            if result.get("status") != ACCEPTED:
                raise ValueError(
                    "snapshot_after must identify an ACCEPTED event; "
                    f"{snapshot_after['symbol']} sequence {snapshot_after['sequence']} "
                    f"was {result.get('status')}"
                )
            exported = export_snapshot(replayer)

    if snapshot_after != "last" and not marker_matched:
        raise ValueError("snapshot_after did not match any event in the stream")
    if snapshot_after == "last":
        exported = export_snapshot(replayer)

    return {"results": results, "snapshot": exported}

1	"""Single-instrument order book with price-time priority matching.
2	
3	The engine is deterministic: given the same sequence of event objects it
4	produces identical results, trade identifiers and book snapshots.
5	Rejected events never mutate engine state.
6	"""

11	import json

14	ADD = "ADD"
15	CANCEL = "CANCEL"
16	REPLACE = "REPLACE"
17	EXECUTION_REPORT = "EXECUTION_REPORT"
18	ACCOUNT_REPORT = "ACCOUNT_REPORT"
19	DAY_END_RECONCILIATION = "DAY_END_RECONCILIATION"
20	BUY = "BUY"

94	    def __init__(self, _state: dict[str, object] | None = None) -> None:
95	        if _state is not None:
96	            # Internal fast path used when restoring an authoritative snapshot:
97	            # the state dict is owned by the caller's snapshot machinery, not by
98	            # user input, so it can be adopted verbatim without copying.
99	            self._event_ids: set[str] = _state["event_ids"]
100	            self._order_ids: set[str] = _state["order_ids"]
101	            self._reserved_order_ids: set[str] = _state["reserved_order_ids"]
102	            self._orders: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = _state["orders"]
103	            self._bids: dict[int, deque[str]] = _state["bids"]
104	            self._asks: dict[int, deque[str]] = _state["asks"]
105	            self._bid_totals: dict[int, int] = _state["bid_totals"]
106	            self._ask_totals: dict[int, int] = _state["ask_totals"]
107	            self._next_trade_id: int = _state["next_trade_id"]
108	            self._accounts: set[str] = _state["accounts"]
109	            self._trade_log: list[dict[str, object]] = _state["trade_log"]
110	            return
111	        self._event_ids = set()
112	        self._order_ids = set()
113	        # Identifiers reserved by future parent-order slices: they block reuse
114	        # through ADD exactly like spent order ids, but have no order record
115	        # until their slice is released. Always empty on the baseline entry
116	        # points.
117	        self._reserved_order_ids = set()
118	        self._orders = {}
119	        self._bids = {}
120	        self._asks = {}
121	        self._bid_totals = {}
122	        self._ask_totals = {}
123	        self._next_trade_id = 1
124	        # Accounts seen on any accepted ADD, however the orders ended up.
125	        self._accounts = set()
126	        # Every trade ever executed, in trade_id order, tagged with the id of
127	        # the event that produced it. Execution reports are built from this
128	        # journal; matching output keeps its historical shape.
129	        self._trade_log = []

131	    def handle_line(self, line: str) -> tuple[str | None, str, str | None, list[dict[str, object]]]:

135	        the event id when it can be obtained as a string, otherwise ``None``,
136	        and ``reason`` is set only for rejected events.
137	        """
138	        event_id, result, reason, trades, _stp = self.handle_line_full(line)
139	        return event_id, result, reason, trades

145	        prevention descriptor (``None`` for every other result)."""
146	        event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, _analysis = self.handle_line_extended(line)

200	        self, obj: object

210	    def handle_object_position(
211	        self, obj: object
212	    ) -> tuple[
213	        str | None, str, str | None,
214	        list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None,
215	        dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None,
216	    ]:
217	        event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, analysis, position, _recon = (
218	            self.handle_object_reconciliation(obj)
219	        )

222	    def handle_object_reconciliation(
223	        self, obj: object
224	    ) -> tuple[
225	        str | None, str, str | None,
226	        list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None,
227	        dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None,
228	        dict[str, object] | None,
229	    ]:
230	        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
231	            return None, REJECTED, INVALID_SCHEMA, [], None, None, None, None
232	
233	        event_id = obj.get("event_id")
234	        event_id_out = event_id if isinstance(event_id, str) else None
235	
236	        schema_error = self._schema_error(obj)
237	        if schema_error is not None:
238	            return event_id_out, REJECTED, schema_error, [], None, None, None, None
239	
240	        if event_id in self._event_ids:
241	            return event_id, REJECTED, DUPLICATE_EVENT_ID, [], None, None, None, None
242	        if obj["type"] == REPLACE and "display_quantity" in obj:
243	            target = self._orders.get(obj["order_id"])
244	            if (
245	                target is not None
246	                and target["status"] == RESTING
247	                and "display_quantity" not in target
248	            ):
249	                # Only an iceberg target may be replaced with a display slice;
250	                # like every schema error this consumes no event id.
251	                return event_id, REJECTED, INVALID_SCHEMA, [], None, None, None, None
252	        # The event is well formed, so its id occupies the stream from here,
253	        # even if a later business rule rejects it.
254	        self._event_ids.add(event_id)
255	
256	        if obj["type"] == CANCEL:
257	            event_id, result, reason, trades = self._cancel(event_id, obj["order_id"])
258	            return event_id, result, reason, trades, None, None, None, None
259	        if obj["type"] == REPLACE:
260	            event_id, result, reason, trades, stp = self._replace(event_id, obj)
261	            return event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, None, None, None
262	        if obj["type"] == EXECUTION_REPORT:
263	            event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, analysis = self._execution_report(
264	                event_id, obj
265	            )
266	            return event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, analysis, None, None
267	        if obj["type"] == ACCOUNT_REPORT:
268	            event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, analysis, position = (
269	                self._account_report(event_id, obj)
270	            )
271	            return event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, analysis, position, None
272	        if obj["type"] == DAY_END_RECONCILIATION:
273	            return self._day_end_reconciliation(event_id, obj)
274	        event_id, result, reason, trades, stp = self._add(event_id, obj)
275	        return event_id, result, reason, trades, stp, None, None, None

277	    @staticmethod
278	    def _schema_error(obj: dict[str, object]) -> str | None:
279	        keys = set(obj)
280	        event_type = obj.get("type")
281	        if event_type == EXECUTION_REPORT:
282	            # A pure query: exactly the four fields, string identifiers and a
283	            # positive integer benchmark (booleans are not integers).
284	            if keys != _REPORT_KEYS:
285	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
286	            if not isinstance(obj.get("event_id"), str):
287	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
288	            if not isinstance(obj.get("order_id"), str):
289	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
290	            if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("benchmark_price")):
291	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
292	            return None
293	        if event_type == ACCOUNT_REPORT:
294	            # A pure query: exactly the four fields, non-empty string
295	            # identifiers and a positive integer mark (booleans are not
296	            # integers).
297	            if keys != _ACCOUNT_REPORT_KEYS:
298	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
299	            if not _is_non_empty_str(obj.get("event_id")):
300	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
301	            if not _is_non_empty_str(obj.get("account_id")):
302	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
303	            if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("mark_price")):
304	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
305	            return None
306	        if event_type == DAY_END_RECONCILIATION:
307	            # A pure read-only query: exactly the four fields, a non-empty
308	            # string event id and the two external record arrays. Identifiers
309	            # must be unique within their array and booleans are not integers.
310	            if keys != _RECONCILIATION_KEYS:
311	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
312	            if not _is_non_empty_str(obj.get("event_id")):
313	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
314	            expected_trades = obj.get("expected_trades")
315	            expected_accounts = obj.get("expected_accounts")
316	            if not isinstance(expected_trades, list):
317	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
318	            if not isinstance(expected_accounts, list):
319	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
320	            seen_trade_ids: set[int] = set()
321	            for item in expected_trades:
322	                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != _EXPECTED_TRADE_KEYS:
323	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
324	                trade_id = item.get("trade_id")
325	                if not _is_positive_int(trade_id) or trade_id in seen_trade_ids:
326	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
327	                seen_trade_ids.add(trade_id)
328	                if not _is_non_empty_str(item.get("maker_order_id")):
329	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
330	                if not _is_non_empty_str(item.get("taker_order_id")):
331	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
332	                if not _is_positive_int(item.get("price")):
333	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
334	                if not _is_positive_int(item.get("quantity")):
335	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
336	            seen_account_ids: set[str] = set()
337	            for item in expected_accounts:
338	                if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != _EXPECTED_ACCOUNT_KEYS:
339	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
340	                account_id = item.get("account_id")
341	                if not _is_non_empty_str(account_id) or account_id in seen_account_ids:
342	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
343	                seen_account_ids.add(account_id)
344	                if not _is_int(item.get("net_position")):
345	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
346	                if not _is_int(item.get("cash_balance")):
347	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
348	            return None
349	        if not keys <= _ALL_KEYS:
350	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
351	        if not isinstance(obj.get("event_id"), str):
352	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
353	
354	        if event_type == CANCEL:
355	            if keys != _CANCEL_KEYS:
356	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
357	            if not isinstance(obj.get("order_id"), str):
358	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
359	            return None
360	
361	        if event_type == REPLACE:
362	            # Side and order type are inherited from the target, so the event
363	            # must not restate them; time-in-force is always GTC.
364	            if not keys >= _REQUIRED_REPLACE_KEYS:
365	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
366	            if not keys <= _ALLOWED_REPLACE_KEYS:
367	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
368	            if not isinstance(obj.get("order_id"), str):
369	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
370	            if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("quantity")):
371	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
372	            if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("price")):
373	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
374	            if "display_quantity" in obj:
375	                display_quantity = obj["display_quantity"]
376	                if (
377	                    not _is_positive_int(display_quantity)
378	                    or display_quantity > obj["quantity"]
379	                ):
380	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
381	            return None
382	
383	        if event_type != ADD:
384	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
385	        if not keys >= _REQUIRED_ADD_KEYS:
386	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
387	
388	        if not isinstance(obj.get("order_id"), str):
389	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
390	        if obj.get("side") not in (BUY, SELL):
391	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
392	        order_type = obj.get("order_type")
393	        if order_type not in (LIMIT, MARKET, ICEBERG):
394	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
395	        if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("quantity")):
396	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
397	        if "account_id" in obj and not (
398	            isinstance(obj.get("account_id"), str) and obj["account_id"] != ""
399	        ):
400	            # The account tag is optional but may only be a non-empty string.
401	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
402	        if order_type != ICEBERG and "display_quantity" in obj:
403	            # Only iceberg orders carry a display slice size.
404	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
405	
406	        if order_type == ICEBERG:
407	            # Iceberg orders are always-priced GTC limit orders whose single
408	            # maximum visible slice must not exceed the total quantity.
409	            if not _is_positive_int(obj.get("price")):
410	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
411	            display_quantity = obj.get("display_quantity")
412	            if not _is_positive_int(display_quantity) or display_quantity > obj["quantity"]:
413	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
414	            tif = obj.get("time_in_force")
415	            if "time_in_force" in obj and tif != GTC:
416	                # Only an omitted field or explicit GTC are accepted.
417	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
418	            return None
419	
420	        if "price" in obj:
421	            price = obj["price"]
422	            if order_type == LIMIT:
423	                if not _is_positive_int(price):
424	                    return INVALID_SCHEMA
425	            elif price is not None:
426	                # MARKET orders must not carry a non-null price.
427	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
428	        elif order_type == LIMIT:
429	            return INVALID_SCHEMA
430	
431	        if "time_in_force" in obj:
432	            tif = obj["time_in_force"]
433	            if tif not in (GTC, IOC, FOK):
434	                # Non-string values and unknown time-in-force values.
435	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
436	            if order_type == MARKET and tif == GTC:
437	                return INVALID_SCHEMA
438	
439	        return None

441	    def _books(self, side: str) -> tuple[dict[int, deque[str]], dict[int, int]]:
442	        """The book and visible totals on which ``side`` rests."""
443	        if side == BUY:
444	            return self._bids, self._bid_totals
445	        return self._asks, self._ask_totals

447	    def _opposite(self, side: str) -> tuple[dict[int, deque[str]], dict[int, int]]:
448	        """The book and visible totals against which ``side`` matches."""
449	        if side == BUY:
450	            return self._asks, self._ask_totals
451	        return self._bids, self._bid_totals

453	    @staticmethod
454	    def _tradable_fn(side: str, limit: int | None):
455	        if side == BUY:
456	            def tradable(price: int) -> bool:
457	                return limit is None or price <= limit
458	        else:
459	            def tradable(price: int) -> bool:
460	                return limit is None or price >= limit
461	        return tradable

463	    def _add(
464	        self, event_id: str, obj: dict[str, object]
465	    ) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None]:
466	        order_id: str = obj["order_id"]
467	        if order_id in self._order_ids or order_id in self._reserved_order_ids:
468	            return event_id, REJECTED, DUPLICATE_ORDER_ID, [], None
469	        self._order_ids.add(order_id)
470	
471	        side: str = obj["side"]
472	        order_type: str = obj["order_type"]
473	        quantity: int = obj["quantity"]
474	        remaining: int = quantity
475	        is_iceberg = order_type == ICEBERG
476	        limit: int | None = obj["price"] if order_type in (LIMIT, ICEBERG) else None
477	        # LIMIT/ICEBERG default to GTC; MARKET keeps its historical
478	        # immediate-or-cancel semantics. MARKET with explicit GTC and ICEBERG
479	        # with any other time-in-force are rejected during schema checks.
480	        tif: str = obj.get("time_in_force") or (
481	            GTC if order_type in (LIMIT, ICEBERG) else IOC
482	        )
483	        display_quantity: int | None = (
484	            obj["display_quantity"] if is_iceberg else None
485	        )
486	        account_id: str | None = obj.get("account_id")
487	        if account_id is not None:
488	            # Any accepted ADD makes its account known, regardless of how the
489	            # order itself ends up.
490	            self._accounts.add(account_id)
491	
492	        # FOK must either match the whole quantity against the pre-event book
493	        # or do nothing at all: no trades, no book change, no trade ids spent.
494	        # The precheck walks the book in the same price-time order a real fill
495	        # would; a resting iceberg offers its full remaining quantity here,
496	        # including reserve that is not part of the visible book totals. A
497	        # same-account resting order reached before the quantity is met aborts
498	        # the event atomically, before any trade could occur.
499	        if tif == FOK:
500	            fok = self._fok_probe(side, limit, quantity, account_id)
501	            if fok is not None:
502	                record: dict[str, object] = {
503	                    "side": side,
504	                    "price": limit,
505	                    "remaining": quantity,
506	                    "status": CANCELLED,
507	                }
508	                if account_id is not None:
509	                    record["account_id"] = account_id
510	                self._orders[order_id] = record
511	                if fok is False:
512	                    return event_id, UNFILLED_CANCELLED, None, [], None
513	                stp = {
514	                    "maker_order_id": fok,
515	                    "taker_order_id": order_id,
516	                    "cancelled_quantity": quantity,
517	                }
518	                return event_id, SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED, None, [], stp
519	
520	        remaining, trades, stp_maker = self._match(
521	            event_id, order_id, side, limit, remaining, account_id
522	        )
523	
524	        record = {"side": side, "price": limit}
525	        if account_id is not None:
526	            record["account_id"] = account_id
527	        stp: dict[str, object] | None = None
528	        if stp_maker is not None:
529	            # The whole leftover is cancelled; the blocking passive order is
530	            # neither traded nor displaced, and no later liquidity is sought.
531	            result = (
532	                PARTIALLY_FILLED_SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED if trades else SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED
533	            )
534	            record["remaining"] = remaining
535	            record["status"] = CANCELLED
536	            stp = {
537	                "maker_order_id": stp_maker,
538	                "taker_order_id": order_id,
539	                "cancelled_quantity": remaining,
540	            }
541	        elif remaining == 0:
542	            result = FILLED
543	            record["remaining"] = 0
544	            record["status"] = FILLED
545	        elif order_type in (LIMIT, ICEBERG) and tif == GTC:
546	            result = PARTIALLY_FILLED_RESTING if trades else RESTING
547	            record["remaining"] = remaining
548	            record["status"] = RESTING
549	            self._rest(
550	                order_id, side, limit, remaining,
551	                display_quantity if is_iceberg else None, record,
552	            )
553	        else:
554	            # IOC leftovers never enter the book; a successful FOK is always
555	            # fully filled by construction of the pre-event availability check.
556	            result = PARTIALLY_FILLED_CANCELLED if trades else UNFILLED_CANCELLED
557	            record["remaining"] = remaining
558	            record["status"] = CANCELLED
559	
560	        self._orders[order_id] = record
561	        return event_id, result, None, trades, stp

563	    def _fok_probe(
564	        self, side: str, limit: int | None, quantity: int, account_id: str | None
565	    ) -> str | bool | None:
566	        """Probe a FOK request against the pre-event book without mutating it.
567	
568	        Returns ``None`` when the whole quantity can be filled, ``False`` when
569	        liquidity runs short, or the id of the first same-account resting order
570	        reached before the quantity could be met. The walk mirrors a real fill:
571	        price-time priority across and within levels, and an exhausted iceberg
572	        slice replenishes at the tail of its level (including the hidden
573	        reserve) before the level is drained. Queues and slice sizes are copied
574	        for the simulation so the live book stays untouched.
575	        """
576	        opposite, _totals = self._opposite(side)
577	        tradable = self._tradable_fn(side, limit)
578	        need = quantity
579	        prices = sorted(opposite, reverse=side == SELL)
580	        for price in prices:
581	            if not tradable(price):
582	                continue
583	            sim_remaining: dict[str, int] = {}
584	            sim_visible: dict[str, int] = {}
585	            queue: deque[str] = deque()
586	            for maker_id in opposite[price]:
587	                maker = self._orders[maker_id]
588	                sim_remaining[maker_id] = maker["remaining"]
589	                if maker.get("visible") is not None:
590	                    sim_visible[maker_id] = maker["visible"]
591	                queue.append(maker_id)
592	            while queue and need > 0:
593	                maker_id = queue.popleft()
594	                maker = self._orders[maker_id]
595	                if account_id is not None and maker.get("account_id") == account_id:
596	                    return maker_id
597	                if maker_id in sim_visible:
598	                    available = sim_visible[maker_id]
599	                else:
600	                    available = sim_remaining[maker_id]
601	                need -= available
602	                sim_remaining[maker_id] -= available
603	                if maker_id in sim_visible:
604	                    sim_visible[maker_id] -= available
605	                    if sim_visible[maker_id] == 0 and sim_remaining[maker_id] > 0:
606	                        # The replenished slice waits behind every order already
607	                        # visible at this level, exactly as in a real fill.
608	                        sim_visible[maker_id] = min(
609	                            maker["display_quantity"], sim_remaining[maker_id]
610	                        )
611	                        queue.append(maker_id)
612	            if need <= 0:
613	                return None
614	        return False
615	
616	    def _match(
617	        self,
618	        event_id: str,
619	        order_id: str,
620	        side: str,
621	        limit: int | None,
622	        remaining: int,
623	        account_id: str | None,
624	    ) -> tuple[int, list[dict[str, object]], str | None]:
625	        """Match ``order_id`` as taker.
626	
627	        Returns its leftover, the trades already produced, and the id of the
628	        first same-account passive order reached (``None`` when matching ended
629	        normally). On a self-trade block no further liquidity is consulted and
630	        the blocking order is left exactly as it was.
631	        """
632	        opposite, totals = self._opposite(side)
633	        tradable = self._tradable_fn(side, limit)
634	
635	        trades: list[dict[str, object]] = []
636	        blocked_by: str | None = None
637	        while remaining > 0:
638	            candidates = [price for price in totals if tradable(price)]
639	            if not candidates:
640	                break
641	            price = min(candidates) if side == BUY else max(candidates)
642	            queue = opposite[price]
643	            while remaining > 0 and queue:
644	                maker_id = queue[0]
645	                maker = self._orders[maker_id]
646	                if account_id is not None and maker.get("account_id") == account_id:
647	                    # No trade, no queue/remaining/slice change; the taker
648	                    # leftover is cancelled by the caller without skipping on.
649	                    blocked_by = maker_id
650	                    return remaining, trades, blocked_by
651	                if maker.get("visible") is not None:
652	                    # A resting iceberg can only trade its current slice; the
653	                    # reserve stays hidden until the slice is exhausted.
654	                    maker_available = maker["visible"]
655	                else:
656	                    maker_available = maker["remaining"]
657	                matched = min(remaining, maker_available)
658	                maker["remaining"] -= matched
659	                remaining -= matched
660	                totals[price] -= matched
661	                trade: dict[str, object] = {
662	                    "trade_id": self._next_trade_id,
663	                    "maker_order_id": maker_id,
664	                    "taker_order_id": order_id,
665	                    "price": price,
666	                    "quantity": matched,
667	                }
668	                trades.append(trade)
669	                self._trade_log.append({**trade, "event_id": event_id})
670	                self._next_trade_id += 1
671	                if maker.get("visible") is not None:
672	                    maker["visible"] -= matched
673	                    if maker["visible"] == 0:
674	                        # The slice leaves the front immediately. With reserve
675	                        # left, the next slice joins behind every order already
676	                        # visible at this price, so this same taker may meet the
677	                        # order again after those orders.
678	                        queue.popleft()
679	                        if maker["remaining"] > 0:
680	                            new_slice = min(
681	                                maker["display_quantity"], maker["remaining"]
682	                            )
683	                            maker["visible"] = new_slice
684	                            totals[price] += new_slice
685	                            queue.append(maker_id)
686	                        else:
687	                            maker["status"] = FILLED
688	                elif maker["remaining"] == 0:
689	                    queue.popleft()
690	                    maker["status"] = FILLED
691	            if not queue:
692	                del opposite[price]
693	                del totals[price]
694	        return remaining, trades, blocked_by
695	
696	    def _rest(
697	        self,
698	        order_id: str,
699	        side: str,
700	        limit: int,
701	        remaining: int,
702	        display_quantity: int | None,
703	        record: dict[str, object],
704	    ) -> None:
705	        """Enter the leftover at the back of its price level's queue."""
706	        own_book, own_totals = self._books(side)
707	        own_book.setdefault(limit, deque()).append(order_id)
708	        if display_quantity is not None:
709	            # Only the first slice enters the book; the rest is reserve.
710	            visible = min(display_quantity, remaining)
711	            record["display_quantity"] = display_quantity
712	            record["visible"] = visible
713	        else:
714	            visible = remaining
715	        own_totals[limit] = own_totals.get(limit, 0) + visible
716	
717	    def _remove_from_book(self, order_id: str, record: dict[str, object]) -> None:
718	        """Remove a resting order's visible quantity from its price level."""
719	        own_book, own_totals = self._books(record["side"])
720	        price = record["price"]
721	        queue = own_book[price]
722	        queue.remove(order_id)
723	        # Book totals hold only the current visible slice of an iceberg; its
724	        # reserve leaves with the order but was never aggregated.
725	        visible = record.get("visible", record["remaining"])
726	        own_totals[price] -= visible
727	        if own_totals[price] == 0:
728	            del own_totals[price]
729	            del own_book[price]

731	    def _replace(
732	        self, event_id: str, obj: dict[str, object]
733	    ) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None]:
734	        order_id: str = obj["order_id"]
735	        record = self._orders.get(order_id)
736	        if record is None or record["status"] != RESTING:
737	            return event_id, REJECTED, UNKNOWN_ORDER, [], None
738	
739	        side: str = record["side"]
740	        # The replacement trades under the target's account; the event itself
741	        # is forbidden from carrying account_id by the schema checks.
742	        account_id: str | None = record.get("account_id")
743	        is_iceberg = "display_quantity" in record
744	        display_quantity = obj.get("display_quantity")
745	        if display_quantity is None:
746	            # An omitted slice size keeps the target's original peak.
747	            display_quantity = record.get("display_quantity")
748	
749	        # Removal, matching and re-resting are one indivisible state change:
750	        # the old remainder leaves the book before the replacement arrives,
751	        # so the new order can never trade against its own previous state.
752	        self._remove_from_book(order_id, record)
753	
754	        price: int = obj["price"]
755	        remaining, trades, stp_maker = self._match(
756	            event_id, order_id, side, price, obj["quantity"], account_id
757	        )
758	
759	        new_record: dict[str, object] = {"side": side, "price": price}
760	        if account_id is not None:
761	            new_record["account_id"] = account_id
762	        stp: dict[str, object] | None = None
763	        if stp_maker is not None:
764	            # The old remainder was already removed and is not restored; the
765	            # replacement is cancelled with whatever it had left.
766	            result = (
767	                PARTIALLY_FILLED_SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED if trades else SELF_TRADE_PREVENTED
768	            )
769	            new_record["remaining"] = remaining
770	            new_record["status"] = CANCELLED
771	            stp = {
772	                "maker_order_id": stp_maker,
773	                "taker_order_id": order_id,
774	                "cancelled_quantity": remaining,
775	            }
776	        elif remaining == 0:
777	            result = FILLED
778	            new_record["remaining"] = 0
779	            new_record["status"] = FILLED
780	        else:
781	            # The replacement is a fresh GTC arrival and always rests.
782	            result = PARTIALLY_FILLED_RESTING if trades else REPLACED
783	            new_record["remaining"] = remaining
784	            new_record["status"] = RESTING
785	            self._rest(
786	                order_id, side, price, remaining,
787	                display_quantity if is_iceberg else None, new_record,
788	            )
789	
790	        # The order id stays occupied: the replacement keeps it and no later
791	        # ADD may reuse it.
792	        self._orders[order_id] = new_record
793	        return event_id, result, None, trades, stp
794	
795	    def _cancel(
796	        self, event_id: str, order_id: str
797	    ) -> tuple[str, str, str | None, list[dict[str, object]]]:
798	        record = self._orders.get(order_id)
799	        if record is None or record["status"] != RESTING:
800	            return event_id, REJECTED, UNKNOWN_ORDER, []
801	
802	        self._remove_from_book(order_id, record)
803	        record["status"] = CANCELLED
804	        record["remaining"] = 0
805	        return event_id, CANCELLED, None, []

807	    def _execution_report(
808	        self, event_id: str, obj: dict[str, object]
809	    ) -> tuple[
810	        str, str, str | None,
811	        list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None,
812	    ]:
813	        """Answer a cumulative execution query without touching any state.
814	
815	        Every trade the order ever took part in is attributed to its original
816	        ``order_id``: replacements keep the id and iceberg replenishment slices
817	        trade under the same maker id, so the journal lookup alone gathers the
818	        full history, whether the order acted as maker or taker.
819	        """
820	        order_id: str = obj["order_id"]
821	        record = self._orders.get(order_id)
822	        if record is None:
823	            return event_id, REJECTED, UNKNOWN_ORDER, [], None, None
824	
825	        side: str = record["side"]
826	        status: str = record["status"]
827	        # A resting order's remaining total includes the iceberg reserve; a
828	        # finished order has nothing open.
829	        open_quantity = record["remaining"] if status == RESTING else 0
830	
831	        attribution: list[dict[str, object]] = []
832	        filled_quantity = 0
833	        executed_notional = 0
834	        for trade in self._trade_log:
835	            if trade["maker_order_id"] == order_id:
836	                role = MAKER
837	                counterparty = trade["taker_order_id"]
838	            elif trade["taker_order_id"] == order_id:
839	                role = TAKER
840	                counterparty = trade["maker_order_id"]
841	            else:
842	                continue
843	            filled_quantity += trade["quantity"]
844	            executed_notional += trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
845	            attribution.append(
846	                {
847	                    "trade_id": trade["trade_id"],
848	                    "role": role,
849	                    "counterparty_order_id": counterparty,
850	                    "event_id": trade["event_id"],
851	                    "price": trade["price"],
852	                    "quantity": trade["quantity"],
853	                }
854	            )
855	
856	        if filled_quantity:
857	            vwap: dict[str, int] | None = {
858	                "numerator": executed_notional,
859	                "denominator": filled_quantity,
860	            }
861	        else:
862	            vwap = None
863	        benchmark_price: int = obj["benchmark_price"]
864	        slippage = executed_notional - benchmark_price * filled_quantity
865	        if side == SELL:
866	            # Mirror the buy formula: negative always means improvement.
867	            slippage = -slippage
868	
869	        analysis: dict[str, object] = {
870	            "side": side,
871	            "current_status": status,
872	            "open_quantity": open_quantity,
873	            "filled_quantity": filled_quantity,
874	            "executed_notional": executed_notional,
875	            "vwap": vwap,
876	            "slippage_notional": slippage,
877	            "trade_attribution": attribution,
878	        }
879	        return event_id, REPORTED, None, [], None, analysis
880	
881	    def _account_report(
882	        self, event_id: str, obj: dict[str, object]
883	    ) -> tuple[
884	        str, str, str | None,
885	        list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None,
886	        dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None,
887	    ]:
888	        """Answer a cumulative account query without touching any state.
889	
890	        Every trade is attributed to an account through the order it was
891	        resting or arriving as: replacements keep the order id and its
892	        account, and iceberg replenishment slices trade under the same maker
893	        id, so the journal lookup alone gathers the full history. Orders
894	        without an ``account_id`` never contribute.
895	        """
896	        account_id: str = obj["account_id"]
897	        if account_id not in self._accounts:
898	            return event_id, REJECTED, UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT, [], None, None, None
899	
900	        buy_quantity = 0
901	        sell_quantity = 0
902	        buy_notional = 0
903	        sell_notional = 0
904	        for trade in self._trade_log:
905	            for order_key in ("maker_order_id", "taker_order_id"):
906	                order = self._orders[trade[order_key]]
907	                if order.get("account_id") != account_id:
908	                    continue
909	                notional = trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
910	                if order["side"] == BUY:
911	                    buy_quantity += trade["quantity"]
912	                    buy_notional += notional
913	                else:
914	                    sell_quantity += trade["quantity"]
915	                    sell_notional += notional
916	
917	        net_position = buy_quantity - sell_quantity
918	        if buy_quantity:
919	            buy_vwap: dict[str, int] | None = {
920	                "numerator": buy_notional,
921	                "denominator": buy_quantity,
922	            }
923	        else:
924	            buy_vwap = None
925	        if sell_quantity:
926	            sell_vwap: dict[str, int] | None = {
927	                "numerator": sell_notional,
928	                "denominator": sell_quantity,
929	            }
930	        else:
931	            sell_vwap = None
932	
933	        mark_price: int = obj["mark_price"]
934	        analysis: dict[str, object] = {
935	            "account_id": account_id,
936	            "mark_price": mark_price,
937	            "buy_quantity": buy_quantity,
938	            "sell_quantity": sell_quantity,
939	            "net_position": net_position,
940	            "buy_notional": buy_notional,
941	            "sell_notional": sell_notional,
942	            "buy_vwap": buy_vwap,
943	            "sell_vwap": sell_vwap,
944	            "turnover_notional": buy_notional + sell_notional,
945	            "risk_exposure": abs(net_position) * mark_price,
946	            "mark_to_market_pnl": (
947	                sell_notional - buy_notional + net_position * mark_price
948	            ),
949	        }
950	        return event_id, REPORTED, None, [], None, None, analysis

952	    def _day_end_reconciliation(
953	        self, event_id: str, obj: dict[str, object]
954	    ) -> tuple[
955	        str, str, str | None,
956	        list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, object] | None,
957	        dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None,
958	        dict[str, object] | None,
959	    ]:
960	        """Compare the cumulative journal against external end-of-day records.
961	
962	        Purely read-only: the book, order states, queue priorities, trade
963	        journal, account set and next trade id are all left untouched. The
964	        actual side is rebuilt from the same journal the reports use, so
965	        replacements and iceberg replenishment slices contribute under their
966	        original order id and inherited account.
967	        """
968	        actual_trades: dict[int, dict[str, object]] = {}
969	        for trade in self._trade_log:
970	            actual_trades[trade["trade_id"]] = {
971	                "trade_id": trade["trade_id"],
972	                "maker_order_id": trade["maker_order_id"],
973	                "taker_order_id": trade["taker_order_id"],
974	                "price": trade["price"],
975	                "quantity": trade["quantity"],
976	            }
977	
978	        # Every account an accepted ADD ever named is part of the actual set,
979	        # whether or not it traded; cash is sell notional minus buy notional.
980	        actual_accounts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {
981	            account_id: {
982	                "account_id": account_id,
983	                "net_position": 0,
984	                "cash_balance": 0,
985	            }
986	            for account_id in self._accounts
987	        }
988	        for trade in self._trade_log:
989	            notional = trade["price"] * trade["quantity"]
990	            for order_key in ("maker_order_id", "taker_order_id"):
991	                order = self._orders[trade[order_key]]
992	                account_id = order.get("account_id")
993	                if account_id is None:
994	                    continue
995	                position = actual_accounts[account_id]
996	                if order["side"] == BUY:
997	                    position["net_position"] += trade["quantity"]
998	                    position["cash_balance"] -= notional
999	                else:
1000	                    position["net_position"] -= trade["quantity"]
1001	                    position["cash_balance"] += notional
1002	
1003	        # The external records are normalized into the same field order the
1004	        # actual side uses, so equal content compares (and serializes) equal.
1005	        expected_trades: dict[int, dict[str, object]] = {}
1006	        for item in obj["expected_trades"]:
1007	            expected_trades[item["trade_id"]] = {
1008	                "trade_id": item["trade_id"],
1009	                "maker_order_id": item["maker_order_id"],
1010	                "taker_order_id": item["taker_order_id"],
1011	                "price": item["price"],
1012	                "quantity": item["quantity"],
1013	            }
1014	        expected_accounts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1015	        for item in obj["expected_accounts"]:
1016	            expected_accounts[item["account_id"]] = {
1017	                "account_id": item["account_id"],
1018	                "net_position": item["net_position"],
1019	                "cash_balance": item["cash_balance"],
1020	            }
1021	
1022	        trade_breaks = self._reconcile_breaks(expected_trades, actual_trades)
1023	        account_breaks = self._reconcile_breaks(expected_accounts, actual_accounts)
1024	        result = RECONCILED if not trade_breaks and not account_breaks else BREAKS_FOUND
1025	        reconciliation: dict[str, object] = {
1026	            "trade_breaks": trade_breaks,
1027	            "account_breaks": account_breaks,
1028	        }
1029	        return event_id, result, None, [], None, None, None, reconciliation
1030	
1031	    @staticmethod
1032	    def _reconcile_breaks(
1033	        expected: dict[object, dict[str, object]],
1034	        actual: dict[object, dict[str, object]],
1035	    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1036	        """Full outer comparison of two identifier-keyed record sets.
1037	
1038	        Breaks are emitted in ascending identifier order; a record present on
1039	        only one side reports the other side as ``None``.
1040	        """
1041	        breaks: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1042	        for identifier in sorted(expected.keys() | actual.keys()):
1043	            exp = expected.get(identifier)
1044	            act = actual.get(identifier)
1045	            if exp is None:
1046	                reason = MISSING_EXPECTED
1047	            elif act is None:
1048	                reason = MISSING_ACTUAL
1049	            elif exp != act:
1050	                reason = FIELD_MISMATCH
1051	            else:
1052	                continue
1053	            breaks.append(
1054	                {
1055	                    "identifier": identifier,
1056	                    "expected": exp,
1057	                    "actual": act,
1058	                    "reason": reason,
1059	                }
1060	            )
1061	        return breaks

1066	            for price in sorted(self._bid_totals, reverse=True)

1081	        Used by parent-order plans: every future slice id is reserved when the
1082	        plan starts, so a later external ADD can never occupy it. Releasing the
1083	        slice moves the id into the regular spent-id set.

1098	    def dump_state(self) -> dict[str, object]:
1099	        """Export the complete mutable engine state for an authoritative owner.
1100
